per_case.answer_text:
Summary — how to vote on OpenChat proposals

1) Join the proposals group and read the governance guide. The proposals group shows current proposals and discussion; the governance blog gives a step‑by‑step overview. (See group and blog links.)

2) Eligibility. To vote a neuron must exist and have a dissolve delay of at least 1 month at the time the proposal was made. You can vote “adopt” or “reject” any proposal using any eligible neurons you own.

3) How your vote is counted. Each neuron’s voting power = stake × dissolve‑delay bonus × age bonus. The dissolve‑delay bonus is 1 at 0 delay and rises linearly to 2 at 1 year. The age bonus is 1 at 0 age and rises to 1.25 at 6 months (age resets to 0 if the neuron starts dissolving). Example: 1000 CHAT, 1 year delay, 6 months age → voting power 2500.

4) Proposal outcome rules. A proposal is adopted if adopt votes exceed reject votes after 4 days or a period of quiet, and adopt votes are at least 3% of total voting power. The vote ends immediately if adopt or reject votes exceed 50% of available voting power. You may still participate during the 4‑day period even if the proposal has already been resolved so the neuron can earn voting rewards.

5) How to vote (from the app / NNS dapp). The easiest current method is from within OpenChat. Before voting you must configure your OpenChat User Id as a hot‑key for the neurons you will use to vote. If your neurons are set to follow the neuron with the longest dissolve delay, adding the OpenChat User Id as a hot‑key to that neuron is sufficient.

Steps to add your OpenChat User Id as a hot‑key:
- In OpenChat: open the main menu → Profile settings → Advanced → copy your User Id.
- In the NNS dapp (https://nns.ic0.app/neurons): sign in → My Neuron Staking → Select Nervous System: OpenChat → select the neuron (select the oldest if others follow it) → Add Hotkey → paste your OpenChat User Id.

(If you made proposals yourself, note that non‑motion proposals trigger automatic SNS actions; rejected proposals incur a 10 CHAT burn on the proposing neuron.)

grade.rationale: The answer closely follows the FAQ and governance blog: it directs users to the proposals group and blog, explains eligibility, voting power, outcome rules, and the hot-key setup and following behavior, all supported by the cited chunks. The included note about non‑motion proposals and the 10 CHAT burn on rejection is also sourced. Citations are relevant and the question is answered appropriately.

per_case.answer_text:
Short version
- The airdrop is 100,000 CHAT split into two pots: 80,000 CHAT distributed proportionally by "shares", and 20,000 CHAT given via a lottery. (blog:chit:3)

How the 80,000 pot works
- You receive 1 share for every 5,000 CHIT you have. Your CHAT from this pot = 80,000 × (your shares) ÷ (total shares across all entrants). Example: 36,500 CHIT → 7 shares; if there are 10,000 total shares you get 80,000 × 7 / 10,000 = 56 CHAT. (blog:chit:3)

How the 20,000 (lottery) pot works
- Originally you got 1 ticket per 25,000 CHIT and three prizes (12k, 5k, 3k). For the end-of-August airdrop the rules were changed: participants with at least 25,000 CHIT or at least a 30‑day streak get one ticket; 10 tickets are drawn and each wins 2,000 CHAT. (blog:chit:3) Note: the 30‑day streak is one of the streak milestones used to earn CHIT. (blog:chit:0)

Other important points
- The total amount of CHAT per airdrop is fixed, so the more users/shares there are the smaller each proportional share will be. (blog:chit:3)
- Your airdrop allocation is determined by your current CHIT balance; that balance is reset to zero after each airdrop. There is an expectation of monthly airdrops of 100,000 CHAT. (blog:chit:4)
- To enter the airdrop you must join the CHIT for CHAT community (which requires either lifetime diamond membership or, when available, a proof‑of‑unique‑personhood credential plus standard diamond membership). (blog:chit:2)

per_case.answer_text:
Voting rewards are awarded as maturity to neurons that participate in voting. For each proposal ballot a neuron’s reward is proportional to its voting power compared with the total voting power of the participating (eligible) neurons. Voting power = stake × dissolve-delay bonus × age bonus (dissolve-delay bonus rises linearly from 1 at 0 delay to 2 at a 1‑year delay; age bonus rises from 1 at 0 age to 1.25 at 6 months). A neuron must have a dissolve delay of at least 1 month when the proposal is made to be eligible.

Rewards are generated at a rate of 2.5% of the total token supply annually, distributed daily (taking into account all ballots that ended that day; if there are none the rewards are carried over). Maturity accumulated can be disbursed (minting CHAT) or staked/auto‑staked. Note that if you fail to vote on a proposal you do not earn voting rewards for that proposal (you can configure neurons to follow trusted voters to avoid missing votes), and it is possible to participate even after a proposal resolves so the neuron can still benefit from voting rewards.

grade.rationale: All claims match the cited governance docs: rewards accrue as maturity, are proportional to voting power (stake × dissolve-delay bonus × age bonus), eligibility requires 1-month dissolve delay, rewards distribute daily with carryover, 2.5% annual rate, maturity disbursement/staking options, no rewards if you don’t vote, and late participation within the window still earns rewards. Citations are relevant to each point.
